ai_generation_trigger: An explicit generation/preparation operation creates or refreshes selected candidates. Normal build/check/bundle does not contact an AI; it consumes accepted saved outputs. Missing/stale inputs diagnose. First-generation UX may combine preparation and build explicitly, but no silent provider call is assumed.
deterministic_build_outputs: Application JavaScript and portable Worker bundle
Schemas and HTTP/MCP/form interfaces derived from owning declarations

shared_record: Minimal declaring unit/source association, relevant source/contract/target fingerprint, effective generator recipe and original produced file identities/locations, with current compatibility state. Keep truthful historical origin distinct from current edited bytes; avoid authored dependency/interface manifests or patch-overlay reconstruction.
shared_controls: Use the controls catalog. Primary implementation files are editable; candidate generation/refinement is isolated and promotion compares current source plus file bytes. Reset/failure preserves current direct edits, not just the original generated bytes. Ordinary builds use current tracked bytes without provider calls. Mutating controls require explicit unit selection; neither retry nor reset deletes current output or widens to other units.

provider_configuration.status: Accepted can.gen.toml version 1, complete runner/model profile pairs and explicit settings/run precedence; adapters remain implementation work.
provider_configuration.proposed_file: Accepted can.gen.toml at the explicitly supplied project root; retained key names earlier proposal history.
provider_configuration.source_owner: .can owns app composition, typed contracts, prompts and optional logical profile references. It need not embed tool binaries or provider/model recipes.
provider_configuration.tooling_owner: Project generation config selects CLI adapter/model and bounded execution preferences, with optional role/named profiles. It is not an app/source/dependency/interface manifest.

provider_configuration.profile_selection: Run profile > owning declaration agent > category default. Then frontend resolves its configured complete pair or shared; Given/When use shared. Unknown explicit profiles diagnose.
provider_configuration.settings_resolution: Explicit --settings file replaces committed can.gen.toml at the supplied project root; per-run fields override selected recipe. No ambient user/local/ancestor search. Runner override requires explicit compatible model. Report origins.
provider_configuration.authentication: Use installed CLI login/authentication and local environment. Do not commit credentials or pass them into generated/browser code.
provider_configuration.model_identity: Runner/CLI and model are separate controls. Pass explicit requested model selection; record adapter/executable version, requested model and actual model/provider reported by the tool when available. Report unknown resolved identity rather than inventing a pin.
provider_configuration.change_semantics: Runner/model/config changes affect future generation/refinement. They do not overwrite current implementation, force an AI call, or by themselves make compatible saved code invalid. Status reports recipe drift; relevant source/contracts/target changes still require compatibility reconciliation.
provider_configuration.api_future: A future API runner may implement the same finite input/candidate-output adapter contract. Direct API integration is out of the current CLI-first scope.
provider_configuration.profile_schema: Complete runner/model pairs; optional finite limits reuse shared limits, without an inheritance graph. Native options belong to the chosen adapter recipe and never cross runners implicitly.

runner_contract.input: Captured owning prompts/contracts/templates, current implementation when refining, target configuration, output file group and finite run settings.
runner_contract.invocation: CLI-specific noninteractive arguments passed as an argv array and prompt stdin/file, never concatenated shell commands. Use the installed tool's supported model/permission controls without requiring a TUI.
runner_contract.workspace: Generation/refinement writes an isolated candidate workspace/file group. Direct authoring-agent edits use ordinary authorized workspace access to primary files; do not infer sandboxing from an adapter name.
runner_contract.result: Stream progress, record attempt/session identity where available, completion/cancellation/exit state and actual output files. Candidate validity comes from file/interface/target checks, not a successful chat message.
runner_contract.limits: One attempt by default, timeout and cancellation control. Optional turn/spend/permission controls only when the adapter can enforce them; unsupported requested controls diagnose rather than pretending they worked.
runner_contract.auth_failure: Missing binary/login, unsupported model, permission prompt or unsupported headless mode yields an actionable failure/needs-attention state and retains current files. No automatic fallback to another tool or unrestricted permissions.
runner_contract.continuation: Resume/recover a specific recorded session only where supported and while the captured request is still applicable. Session recovery, explicit retry and new refinement remain distinct.

implementation_files.ownership: Track directly editable generated JS/CSS and required source association/interface metadata as primary implementation inputs. Ignore transient candidate workspaces and logs; exact file locations remain proposed.
implementation_files.example_layout: can.generated/<opaque-unit-id>/unit.json plus server.js, browser.js, style.css, contributions.can and assets only where required. Candidates/logs/leases/journals are ignored under .can/gen/.
implementation_files.direct_editing: The authoring agent inspects/edits current JS/CSS through ordinary authorized file access under brief edit leases. Builds consume actual current bytes with deterministic checks and no AI/candidate ceremony for source-compatible edits.
implementation_files.discovery: Structured inspect/status returns unit IDs, owning source range, current/candidate paths, target, drift/recipe and attempt state. Inline scopes need no name/editor selection; edit.begin returns exact coordinated paths/token.
implementation_files.provenance: Generation records identify the historical output that was actually produced. Later byte edits are marked modified since generation; do not credit them to the original generator or infer an editor identity. Current code and original receipt are distinct facts.
implementation_files.refine: Capture current files plus owning intent/contracts and a refinement instruction, then produce a separate candidate. This preserves manual refinements as input rather than starting from the original generated base.
implementation_files.fresh: An explicit fresh generation starts from the current source prompt/contracts without treating existing edited implementation as the design baseline. It still writes a candidate and does not delete current files.
implementation_files.promotion: Accepted cooperative write leases/build snapshots gate one selected-unit journal over atomic per-file replacements. Compare capture/current bytes/fence; recover unresolved groups before consumption. BGEN10 explicitly excludes uncooperative-writer CAS.
implementation_files.source_repair: Contract/intent drift may be repaired through AI refinement or direct code changes. An explicit deterministic validate/adopt operation can reconcile manually repaired files with current relevant inputs; it does not rewrite historical generation provenance or prove prose meaning.
implementation_files.durable_refinement: If a refinement changes lasting intended behavior/style, update the owning .can prompt/contract or retain the instruction as an explicit refinement note. Current edited code remains saved even when intent has not yet been reconciled; fresh generation is deliberately a new candidate.

controls_catalog.meaning: Check configured adapter availability/version, supported headless/model controls and usable native authentication where deterministically available, without generating code.
Return structured units/IDs, source mapping, concrete current/candidate paths, target, drift, recipe and attempt state; no interactive unit picker required.

Prepare explicitly selected units. UNIT --fresh deliberately requests a new design candidate for that unit without deleting current output. Any app/batch request explicitly lists its affected units; no implicit widening from a selected unit.

Require one explicit unit/attempt target; retry its captured failed attempt only. Preserve current selected output and every unselected unit. No implicit all-failed/app/dependency retry. Different inputs/recipe need a new capture; unknown outcomes use recovery where supported.
Use current implementation and current owning source/contract as the baseline for an AI candidate; optional per-run profile/tool/model override is recorded.
Return machine-readable diffs and optional rendered preview URLs/images/results without replacing current code. Visual/editor UI is optional; no human review gate.

Run finite interface/contract and actual-target checks for a candidate or directly repaired files. Adoption binds manually reconciled files to current inputs without a provider call; exact command spelling and metadata mechanics remain open.

Agent-callable conditional promotion of the selected qualified file group; proposed --accept can combine generation/refinement, checks and promotion. Preserve current files on input/byte/attempt conflict; no required human confirmation.
Stop the runner best-effort and fence late results from promotion; distinguish confirmed stop from unknown provider work.
Discard/supersede pending candidate/attempt state for the selected unit only; preserve its current JS/CSS/direct edits and every other unit. No AI call.
Explicitly restore an earlier tracked implementation/metadata revision with compatibility checking, normally through source-control history.
Consume current tracked implementations and derived dependencies/interfaces, validate and bundle, with zero AI calls and no generation credentials required.

targeting.status: Human-required outcome: independently retry/refine selected units without deleting or changing other units or current selected output.
targeting.granularity: Each explicit style block is its own generation unit; trait, scenario implementation and custom view have separate owning units. Output files are associated with that unit, not one app-wide AI output.
targeting.selection: Require an unambiguous target for retry/refine/fresh/reset/cancel/accept/adopt/rollback. A bare mutating command diagnoses a missing target rather than assuming all units.
targeting.inline: Structured status/inspect resolves a stable internal unit ID from source ownership/location. Inline blocks do not require editor selection or an author-written name; a transient ordinal is not a saved identity.
targeting.isolation: Selected generation writes only the selected unit's candidate file group. Candidate acceptance replaces only that matching group. Unselected unit files/metadata and current code remain intact.
targeting.batch: An explicit target list or explicit batch request must enumerate the affected units before generation. Never widen a retry to the app, all failed attempts or a dependency closure implicitly.
targeting.dependencies: Revalidate relevant consumers when warranted, but do not regenerate or mutate their implementation implicitly. If changes outside selection are required, report the exact dependency and leave those units intact.
targeting.style_scope: Generated selectors/hooks must be scoped to the owning style block; targeted retry cannot modify global theme/shared stylesheet or neighboring units. Nested scope/cascade and shared-view visual dependencies still need a precise implementation contract.
targeting.shared_views: A reusable view definition is a shared unit affecting its instances; structured inspect/diff reports the affected-use set for agent selection and qualification.
targeting.one_large_block: A style block containing two regions is one unit. Strict independent generation control requires separate sibling/nested scopes with defined boundaries; a prose request to preserve part of one scope is not a byte-preservation guarantee.
targeting.example: Keep TaskEntry as-is; generate/refine only TaskList. Selected existing CSS is retained until its replacement candidate is accepted, and TaskEntry never participates in that attempt.

operator_contract.status: Human-required: generation tooling is primarily operated by the AI coding agent authoring .can, not by a person using a generation UI.
operator_contract.primary_surface: Accepted can gen version 1 JSON dispatcher from stdin or --request FILE; one final envelope and optional JSONL events. Explicit IDs and typed errors; no dashboard/picker required.
operator_contract.discovery: Structured inspect/status returns stable unit identity, owner/source location, kind/target, current/candidate file paths, effective generator recipe, drift and attempt state. Inline scope selection is machine-discoverable; names remain optional.
operator_contract.requests: Support explicit unit IDs and instruction/request files or stdin for large structured inputs; CLI arguments remain programmatic argv, not interpolated shell text.
operator_contract.errors: Return typed failures with the concrete affected unit, retained current files, retry/resume capability and bounded next actions. Missing/ambiguous targets or unsupported controls do not trigger interactive guesses.
operator_contract.acceptance: Accepted accept=true composition of generate/refine, validation and selected-unit conditional promotion under write/read leases and journaling, with distinct candidate/accepted outcomes and no human review gate.
operator_contract.inspection: Diff and optional preview artifacts are machine-consumable diagnostics. A graphical editor or person viewing a preview is not a prerequisite to acceptance.
operator_contract.permissions: Honor the authoring/generation task workspace permissions. Adapter authentication/permission needs return structured needs-attention state; headless operation does not silently disable the CLI's controls.
operator_contract.bounded_execution: Agent orchestration can retry/resume/refine with finite attempt/time limits. Failed validation, contract gaps, concurrent edits or unselected dependency requirements leave current files intact and return precise actionable state.
operator_contract.scope: This is the developer generation-control surface. Existing generated application interaction contracts remain owned by Then/UI; no product UI behavior is changed by this decision.
operator_contract.implementation_status: The machine protocol, stable inline identities, adapters and generated-JS validation interface are not implemented. The no-required-human-UI constraint is settled.
